hero.intro: Students, graduates, consultants, and lab-techs in more than 100 countries, on six continents. Here is what we have been doing, where, and when.

posts.title: Accelerator Workshop at Wild Ken Hill
posts.body: Our ten-day Accelerator Workshop ran from 15 to 26 June 2026 at Wild Ken Hill, a regenerative farm and rewilding estate on the Norfolk coast. All 25 places sold out.
posts.people: Led by our Advanced Program mentors

imgs.alt: Fields and hedgerows at Wild Ken Hill, Norfolk

posts.note: The mockup carried 39 photographs and clips from these ten days as Google Drive links, still in HEIC and MOV. They belong on the story page instead, converted, at public/assets/community/. Linnea supplies the files; the story page holds the slots.

posts.title: Our first Permaculture Design Certification cohort begins
posts.body: The school launched its first Permaculture Design Certification course. The next cohort starts on 16 September 2026.

posts.title: A Living Legacy: four webinars in honour of Dr. Elaine
posts.body: Longtime students of Dr. Elaine shared how her research shaped their own work, in a free four-part webinar series.
posts.people: With Daniel Tyrkiel and Adam Swann, Todd Harrington, Celine Basset, Nick Tomasini, Vivian Kaloxilos, and Jo Tobias

imgs.alt: Daniel Tyrkiel and Adam Swann presenting in the webinar series

posts.title: Soil Health Week in Karachi and Sindh
posts.body: Consultant Nick Padwick of Wild Soils UK and the TrashIt team ran six days of talks, farm visits, and compost demonstrations for more than 600 people from 60 districts. They taught at Karachi University, Habib University, and Sindh Agriculture University, and hosted the first Farmers' Baithak at Rahuki Farms in Hyderabad, with growers from seven districts. TrashIt's founders studied with us on scholarship, and TrashIt has since opened a soil microbiology lab.
posts.people: With Nick Padwick and the TrashIt team

imgs.alt: Nick Padwick teaching soil biology at Karachi University

posts.title: Nick Padwick and Daniel Tyrkiel in The Guardian
posts.body: The Guardian featured mentor Nick Padwick, who now grows wheat in a biologically healthy system for a premium market, and graduate Daniel Tyrkiel, who runs microbiology field trials with University of Manchester researcher Dr. Janice Lake.

posts.title: Our June workshop on Nick Padwick's farm
posts.body: Mentor Nick Padwick hosted our June workshop on the regenerative farm he runs in the UK. One student, Melita Coggins, called it a life changing experience.

posts.title: Workshop in Costa Rica
posts.body: Mentor Gerald Ramirez showed students how to make biological liquid amendments, and students and mentors spent long sessions at the microscope together.

imgs.alt: Mentor Gerald Ramirez demonstrating liquid amendments in Costa Rica
Students and mentors at microscopes in Costa Rica

posts.title: Our 2024 graduates
posts.body: 107 people earned the lab-tech title in 2024, and 28 finished our consultant and grower programs. Our 50th consultant finished the program this year.
posts.people: Congratulations to Alex Yakaumo, Anton de Jager, Declan Ramsay, Kent Holle, Kevin Chee, Leslie Lewis, Nick Padwick, Robbin Pott, Vera Dorzhinova, Dora Taklec, Stefan Nieuwenhuijsen, Nathalie Sequeira, Arved Meinzer, Joshua Stone, Mario Villamiel, Wes Sanders, Niels de Jong, Wendy Mickle, Kyle Babcock, Jeroen Boss, Nicolas Rondeau, Reinhard Leeb, Jana Paskova, Julian Ravenscroft, Mary Beerman, Dorota Romanowski, Bianca Lech, and Richard Oosthuysen

posts.title: Compost workshop in Costa Rica
posts.body: Students from our consultant and grower programs came together for a hands-on workshop on making biologically complete compost.

posts.title: Workshop in Mexico with Ecosystem Restoration Camps
posts.body: We ran a workshop in Mexico together with Ecosystem Restoration Camps.
